info.desc: BEYONCÉ is the eponymous fifth solo studio album by American singer Beyoncé. The record was released on December 13, 2013, by Parkwood Entertainment and Columbia Records. Developed as a "visual album", its songs are accompanied by non-linear short films that illustrate the musical concepts conceived during production. Its dark, intimate subject material includes feminist themes of sex, monogamous love, and relationship issues, inspired by Beyoncé's desire to assert her full creative freedom. The album's initial recording began in New York City, where Beyoncé invited producers and songwriters to live with her for a month. During extensive touring the following year, .

podcast.body: A self-titled album released by Beyoncé on Friday, June 10, 2013, as a surprise. This unconventional Friday release date, before the establishment of the global release day, gave her a strategic head start over other artists for chart sales, as it allowed her first chart week to include Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and Monday, thereby artificially inflating her initial sales figures. "She decided to mess things up with a surprise release of a self titled album on June 10, 2013, which was a Friday."

podcast.body: This "game-changing self-title 2013 album" was noted for having "invented the surprise album drop" and was universally acclaimed. Despite its impact and acclaim, it lost the Album of the Year Grammy to Beck's "Morning Phase" in 2015. This marked the first of three consecutive Album of the Year nominations for Beyoncé that did not result in a win. "Beyoncé's game-changing self-title 2013 album, one that, as we discussed in a prior hit parade episode, had invented the surprise album drop, lost the album of the year Grammy to Beck."
